steps.what: Assess circumstances and decide what altitude or route change to request
Request changes from air traffic control and confirm the resulting clearance

tasks.design: The pilot assesses the circumstances and makes the request through {OTHER}, the aircraft radio or approved communications equipment. Clearance interpretation and confirmation remain direct pilot work.
tasks.previous_blocker: The safe request depends on the actual flight and current clearance.
tasks.enabler_now: No evidenced change removes situational judgement or operational communication.
tasks.still_hard: Rapidly changing weather, traffic and ambiguous communications.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding what to request and recognising when a response needs clarification.
tasks.altitude: Operational responsibility and communication authority remain unchanged.

reach.task: Communicate the reason and urgency of a requested change clearly

evidence.claim: Requesting an operational change and confirming its clearance remain human communication and judgement in this scenario.

assumptions: Boundary is assessment and communication of a change request, excluding initial route planning and execution of aircraft manoeuvres.
The pilot observes the circumstances in s1. Air traffic control produces the response during s2 after the request; no clearance is assumed in advance.
No structured safe-route flag, automated request or generated phraseology is introduced. Unclear responses use existing clarification procedures.
Native approved communications remain the first option; no custom tool is proposed.
Zero incremental upkeep because the existing process is unchanged.
unknowns: Operation type and approved communication methods
research_questions: What proportion of change-request time is operational judgement and clearance clarification rather than avoidable administration?

already_counted.description: Decision and clearance communication remain fully counted

incremental.description: No new tool or process to maintain

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net saving 0. The scenario retains actual change-request judgement and communication without inventing a paperwork step.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Check final instrument flight plan and capture required filing particulars
Copy checked particulars into the instrument flight plan filing form
Verify the exact filing message and file the instrument flight plan
Check filing acknowledgement and resolve rejection or amendment requirements

tasks.design: Configure native prefill in {OTHER}, the approved flight-planning and filing application, from pilot-checked particulars. The pilot verifies and submits the exact message, then checks acknowledgement; no model chooses a route or treats filing acceptance as a clearance.
tasks.previous_blocker: Final plan particulars may be retyped into a separate filing form.
tasks.enabler_now: Deterministic field mapping can prepare a draft message where the existing application supports native prefill.
tasks.still_hard: Correct aircraft capabilities, current plan versions and rejection or amendment handling.
tasks.human_edge: Confirming that the filed message accurately represents the intended flight.
tasks.altitude: The pilot may avoid repeated typing while retaining filing responsibility and all acknowledgement checks.

reach.task: Reconcile filed-message versions and amendment status
reach.learn: Filing syntax, service responses and operator escalation

evidence.claim: Native form prefill from checked flight-plan fields is plausible; the digest does not establish this exact filing integration or its labour saving.
The digest reports a flight-planning system failure with widespread disruption, supporting explicit rejection and failure handling rather than assuming a transmitted message succeeded.

assumptions: Boundary begins with a final plan from the existing pilot planning process and ends with confirmed filing status. Plan creation, air traffic clearance and flying are outside this task and receive no additional savings here.

The pilot produces the final plan in the preceding unchanged planning task. In s1 the pilot checks or captures aircraft ID, flight rules and type, aircraft type and wake category, equipment and capabilities, departure place and time, speed, level, route, destination, duration, alternates and applicable supplementary particulars, plus plan version and filing recipient. All missing-field capture is counted in s1.

S2 maps only confirmed fields; absent capability details, ambiguous routing or stale versions return to manual preparation. The pilot checks meaning and completeness in s3 before transmission, not just message syntax.
The filing service produces its response after s3 and before s4. Rejection, timeout or any amendment requires the existing manual process and renewed approval of the exact changed message.
Test native prefill first. If the application already prepares the message, incremental saving is zero; existing network transmission runtime is not pilot labour.

Allow 8 focal hours per 100 baseline for mapping updates, failed preparation and sample comparison; allow 2 other-role hours for access/configuration upkeep. Operator approval and national consultation requirements are customer facts.
unknowns: Existing native prefill and actual retyping baseline
Filing interfaces and operator validation requirements
research_questions: Does prefill save hands-on time after full content review, rejection handling and comparison with the final plan?

already_counted.description: Plan checking and missing filing-particular capture remain counted
Exact message review, submission and response handling remain counted

incremental.description: Maintain field mappings and handle preparation failures and sample checks

approvals.approved_version: Exact final filing message, plan version, aircraft, date/time and filing recipient; any altered field, recipient or amendment voids approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=70; gross saving 30 less 8 focal upkeep gives net 22. Range 3-12 assumes separate manual retyping remains and amendments and failed prefill consume part of the gain; existing automatic prefill yields zero additional saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Instruct pilots and student pilots through explanation, demonstration and supervised aircraft operations
Debrief the learner and identify aircraft operation skills needing further practice

tasks.design: Keep aircraft instruction and debriefing with the qualified instructor. Existing objectives in {LMS}, where used, can support the session but do not replace demonstration, supervision or learner feedback.
tasks.previous_blocker: Training requires observing actual behaviour and adapting instruction safely.
tasks.enabler_now: No supported change removes direct teaching time.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising misunderstanding, intervening appropriately and building reliable operational judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Responsive teaching and responsibility for supervised practice.
tasks.altitude: The instructor's teaching responsibilities and authority remain unchanged.

reach.task: Identify suitable follow-up practice from an instructor debrief
reach.learn: Training sequence and instructor qualification boundaries

evidence.claim: Direct instruction, observation and responsive debrief remain substantive instructor work.

assumptions: Boundary is qualified instruction and debrief, excluding separate lesson-material production, scheduling and formal proficiency examinations.
The existing training programme supplies objectives before s1. Learner actions during s1 produce observed performance, which is available for s2; no structured proficiency score is assumed.
All observation and feedback capture needed for the debrief is included in retained instruction time. Missing evidence requires more observation, not model inference.
Consider native learning-system functions before custom tools for a distinct administrative need; no build is proposed.
Zero incremental upkeep because instruction remains unchanged.
unknowns: Actual mix of ground, simulator and aircraft teaching
research_questions: Is any separate preparation or recording workload material enough to study without reducing supervised practice?

already_counted.description: Instruction and learner debrief remain fully counted

incremental.description: No new software or process to maintain

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net saving 0. The scenario retains actual pilot instruction and debrief rather than assuming unrelated content-generation work.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Fly with pilots or pilot-license applicants and observe their proficiency
Evaluate observed proficiency against criteria and communicate the assessment result

tasks.design: Retain the qualified examiner's in-flight observation and proficiency decision. Criteria may be stored in {DOCS}, but software does not infer a pass from incomplete observations or replace the flight assessment.
tasks.previous_blocker: Assessment concerns real performance and operational judgement under actual test conditions.
tasks.enabler_now: No evidenced change removes observation or examiner responsibility.
tasks.still_hard: Interpreting inconsistent performance fairly while maintaining flight safety.
tasks.human_edge: Direct observation and accountable evaluation against the required standard.
tasks.altitude: The examiner retains assessment authority and the full in-flight evaluation workload.

reach.task: Explain observed skill gaps for follow-up training without changing the examination result
reach.learn: Assessment standards, evidence limits and role separation

evidence.claim: In-flight proficiency observation and an examiner's assessment remain human work; no automated scoring capability or saving is asserted.

assumptions: Boundary is this qualified pilot's examination activity, excluding licensing authority processing and routine instruction counted separately.

The applicable assessment body supplies criteria before the flight. The applicant produces actual performance during s1 and the examiner records observations within that fully retained step; the result is produced only in s2.
No pre-existing structured pass/fail flag or free automated observation feed is assumed. Insufficient evidence follows the applicable assessment process rather than a generated judgement.
Test existing assessment records before custom tools for separate paperwork; no system change is proposed.
Zero incremental upkeep because the assessment process remains unchanged.
unknowns: Examiner qualification and applicable assessment process
research_questions: How is sufficient evidence for each proficiency criterion established in the present examination process?

already_counted.description: Flight observation and accountable proficiency decision remain fully counted

incremental.description: No new scoring system or process to maintain

approvals.approved_version: Exact applicant, flight/test identification, observation set and final proficiency result; any change requires renewed examiner assessment

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net saving 0. The scenario retains in-flight observation, evaluation and feedback rather than substituting a generated proficiency score.
